title: A Free K-Goods Expo at Seoul's DDP You Can Just Walk Into (Nov 20–22)
html:
If you're going to be in Seoul between November 20 and 22, 2026, here's a fun, free, and totally low-commitment stop to add to your trip: The Souvenir Fair (대한민국 관광기념품 박람회), a government-run expo celebrating Korean souvenirs and gifts — what locals call "K-goods" — held right in the heart of one of Seoul's most photographed buildings.

What Is the Souvenir Fair?

This is an annual exhibition organized by Korea's Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism and the Korea Tourism Organization, where around 140 companies — big brands and small local makers alike — set up booths to show off Korean souvenirs, from traditional crafts to trendy modern gift items. A highlight is a special display of the 25 award-winning designs from this year's national souvenir design competition, plus a section dedicated to souvenirs from other countries for comparison.

It's not a sit-and-watch kind of event — you walk through the hall at your own pace, browse the booths, and in many cases buy directly from the makers on the spot. Think of it as a cross between a trade show and a pop-up gift market.

When, Where, and How Much It Costs

The fair runs November 20–22, 2026, from 10:00 to 19:00 (10:00–18:00 on the final day, with last admission 30 minutes before closing). It's held at Art Hall 1 & 2 of Dongdaemun Design Plaza, usually just called "DDP" — a huge, curvy, futuristic building designed by architect Zaha Hadid that's a landmark in its own right, even if you're not there for the fair. Admission is completely free, no ticket or registration needed.

Good to know for first-timers: "DDP" sits in the Dongdaemun area, which is also known for 24-hour wholesale fashion markets and street food stalls, so it's easy to turn this into a half-day out rather than a quick in-and-out stop.

Getting There From Central Seoul

The easiest way in is the subway: get off at Dongdaemun History & Culture Park Station, served by Line 2, Line 4, and Line 5, and take the exit marked for DDP (Exit 1 is the most commonly used one) — the building's entrance is right there, no long walk required. If you're coming from Myeongdong or Hongdae, it's a direct ride with no transfer on Line 4 or Line 2 for many starting points.

One local habit worth copying: Koreans visiting expos like this tend to go on a weekday afternoon rather than the weekend, when it can get noticeably more crowded with families and group tours — worth keeping in mind if you'd rather browse at a relaxed pace.

💬 Planning to swing by DDP for this one, or have questions about getting there? Drop a comment below — happy to help!
meta_description: A free souvenir expo at Seoul's DDP, Nov 20-22, 2026 — 140+ brands, award-winning K-goods designs, and easy subway access.
